data.title: Last day to buy Tech Mahindra shares for bonus eligibility: Key details
data.description:
Tech Mahindra bonus shares record date:Tech Mahindra shares are in focus on Friday (November 27), as today is the last day for investors to buy the IT company's shares and qualify for its 1:1 bonus issue. 
 
Under the 1:1 bonus issue, eligible shareholders will receive one additional fully paid-up equity share of ₹5 face value for every existing equity share of ₹5 held by them.
 
For instance, an investor holding 100 shares of Tech Mahindra will receive another 100 shares, taking the total holding to 200 shares. However, a bonus issue does not increase the value of an investor's holding.
 
Tech Mahindra share price will adjust proportionately to factor in the increase in the number of outstanding shares in the secondary market. The share price will be adjusted to half of its pre-bonus level on the record date.
 
 
In an exchange filing dated November 23, Tech Mahindra said that it has fixed November 30 (Monday) as the record date for determining shareholder eligibility for the bonus issue.
 
Accordingly, under the T+1 settlement cycle, Friday is the last day to purchase Tech Mahindra shares and become eligible for the bonus issue. 
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex slumps 600 pts, Nifty tests 25,700; Nifty Defence up 3%
 
Investors buying the shares on or after November 30 will not qualify for the bonus issue.
 
Tech Mahindra also informed that December 1 has been fixed as the date of allotment of the bonus shares. The newly issued shares will become available for trading on the stock exchanges, starting December 2.
 
Tech Mahindra shares traded nearly 1 per cent lower at ₹1,839 on Friday around 11:45 AM.
 
Tech Mahindra is a leading IT services company. According to NSE data, its shares have gained 15 per cent so far in 2026 and 23 per cent over the past one year.
 
For the July-September quarter of FY2026-27, the Pune-based company reported a 32.74 per cent Y-o-Y increase in consolidated net profit to ₹1,585.6 crore. Its revenue from operations rose 15.6 per cent to ₹16,180.2 crore.

data.title: Pak intruder shot dead by BSF troops along international border in Punjab
data.description:
Border Security Force (BSF) troops shot dead a Pakistani intruder along the International Border with Pakistan in Punjab on Friday, officials said.

They said the man was shot dead around 2 am in the Pahadpur border post area along the Ujh River in Pathankot.

The intruder was challenged and asked to stop, but he continued moving towards the International Border (IB) and was shot by the BSF troops, the officials said.

The BSF guards the India-Pakistan IB.

Further details are awaited.

data.title: SC refuses urgent listing of plea against Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana
data.description:
The Supreme Court on Friday declined to list for urgent hearing a petition challenging the release of the Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, saying anyone with a different view of the epic is free to make a film of their own.

A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed that the film is already running in theatres and that those who wanted to watch it have already done so.

The petitioner's counsel told the court that the plea had been registered on November 23 and was yet to be listed for hearing.

"The movie has already been released. Those who wanted to watch it have already seen it," the CJI said. When the counsel argued that "many facts have been distorted" in the film, Justice Bagchi said, "They made a movie as they understand, you make a movie as you understand. Don't waste the time of the court. If you have a counter view about the epic, make a movie based on that." As the lawyer pressed for an early hearing, the bench said the matter would be listed in due course.

 

The petition alleges that the makers distorted mythological facts in their depiction of the epic.

Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, also referred to as Ramayana: Part 1, is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra.

It brings the epic to the big screen with Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, and Yash as Ravana.

The ensemble cast includes Sunny Deol, Ravie Dubey, Lara Dutta, Arun Govil, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh and Vivek Oberoi. The film was released in theatres on November 5, 2026.

data.title: Titan, TBZ: Jewellery, gold financiers' stocks rise as bullion rebounds 2%
data.description:
Gold-linked stocks were trading higher on Friday after a marginal recovery in bullion prices following the recent sharp correction. Today’s rally lifted sentiment towards jewellery makers and gold-financing companies. The rebound follows multiple sessions of weakness, with gold futures on the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) slipping to trade around ₹1.22 lakh per 10 grams, a decline of about 30 per cent from start of the year peak.
 
However, on Friday the December MCX gold future was trading over 2 per cent higher at ₹1.24 lakh per 10 grams. Similarly, Gold spot price was trading 2.92 per cent higher at $3,638.90
 
At the last check, shares of Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri was trading 5 per cent higher at  566.30, while Manappuram Finance gained 1.8 per cent to ₹275.05. Meanwhile, industry leader Titan’s share price was trading 1.4 per cent higher. Similarly, Kalyan Jewellers’ share price was also trading 1.7 per cent higher on Friday.
 
 
Sunny Agrawal, head, fundamental research at SBI Securities, said that, because of a mild recovery in gold prices, gold financiers and jewellery players are witnessing a relief rally. “Jewellery players are looking forward to the wedding season, and with a sharp correction in gold and silver prices, volume growth should be robust, and discounting on making charges should come off,” he added. 
 
Kaveri More, commodity technical analyst at Choice Broking, said that Gold prices have staged a strong recovery from the recent low of $3,426.80 and are currently hovering around $3,633 on the COMEX, while MCX gold is trading near ₹124,300, marking an almost 5 per cent recovery from the lows. Silver has also witnessed a sharp rebound, rising from a low of $38.19 to around $43.50 on the COMEX, while MCX silver is trading near ₹151,650, reflecting a recovery of nearly 10 per cent. 
 
“The rebound in bullion prices has been supported by lower-level buying and short-covering, alongside a weaker US dollar and improving sentiment around the technology sector. However, expectations of continued Federal Reserve monetary tightening remain a key factor that could limit further upside. Overall, the recovery indicates improved buying interest, although price movements may remain sensitive to the dollar and Fed policy expectations,” she added. 
  
Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Australia's new digital law could cost Big Tech billions: Here's how
data.description:
After implementing a world-first social media ban for children under 16, Australia has passed another major online safety law, requiring technology companies to proactively prevent harmful content and features on their platforms or face billion-dollar fines.
 
On Wednesday, the Australian Parliament passed the Digital Duty of Care Bill, 2026, making online services, including games, apps, social media platforms and AI chatbots, legally responsible for protecting users from harm.
 
Companies violating the law face fines of up to 5 per cent of their global turnover or A$109.2 million, whichever is greater.
 
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described the Digital Duty of Care law as the next step in Australia's efforts to improve online safety. "It's about Australia taking action on the side of parents and children, not foreign-owned tech companies," he told Parliament, according to Time magazine.
 
 
What does Australia's Digital Duty of Care law say?
 
The law places a legal duty on online services to protect users from serious harm. Platforms will have to assess risks arising from the way their services are designed and operated, rather than simply responding to complaints or removing harmful content after it appears. The eSafety Commissioner will be responsible for enforcing the law.
 
The law amends the Online Safety Act, 2021, replacing the existing collection of online safety codes, standards and Basic Online Safety Expectations with a single, enforceable duty of care.
 
The legislation identifies several categories of harm, including child sexual exploitation, explicit threats of violence and encouragement of terrorism.
 
Under the new law, platforms must submit risk assessments to regulators at least once a year. They must also notify regulators before introducing significant changes to their platforms that could create new risks of harm, including through potentially 'addictive' design features.
 
The law also introduces stronger privacy protections for users, expands regulatory powers to remove 'nudifying' services and clarifies the definition of 'hostile attitudes to women'. This refers to material depicting hatred or the inferiority of women, or promoting violence, abuse, exclusion or the denial of women's rights.
 
One key provision of the legislation is the steep financial penalty for violations. Companies that breach the law face fines of up to 5 per cent of their global turnover or A$109.2 million ($72 million), whichever is greater. Since major technology platforms typically generate annual revenues worth hundreds of billions of dollars, the maximum penalties could reach tens of billions of dollars.
 
What does the law mean for users?
 
The law introduces a feature called 'My Feed, My Way', which will give users greater control over the content they see on platforms.
 
Instead of relying on algorithms to determine what appears on their feeds based on what they watch or engage with, users will be able to choose to see content from accounts they follow.
 
The amendments also make it easier for Australian citizens to hold technology companies accountable. Previously, individuals had to rely on complex legal avenues involving company negligence and consumer protection.
 
The new law grants Australians a 'private right of action', allowing them to directly sue digital platforms for breaching their duty of care. They will be able to take a platform to court, individually or as a group, for breaches that cause them loss or damage.
 
Why has the US raised concerns over the law?
 
Since the legislation applies to several US-based technology companies, the US has argued that vaguely defined 'harms,' backed by penalties of up to 5 per cent of global revenue, could push platforms to censor lawful speech.
 
In a post on X, US Ambassador David Brat said free speech was the foundation of a free society and that protecting it was a US priority. He said he outlined the Trump administration's objections to the Digital Duty of Care law to Australian Communications Minister Anika Wells.
 
Meanwhile, the Tech Council of Australia, an industry body whose members include Google, Microsoft and LinkedIn, said it supported the law but raised concerns about the amendments.

data.title: Tax buoyancy slips, was above 1 in just four of 28 states in FY25
data.description:
On every purchase, from groceries to a movie ticket, a share goes to the government as tax. For a state, own tax revenue (OTR) is the income it raises through its own taxes rather than relying on central government transfers or grants. It is a yardstick of a state’s fiscal strength.
 
That yardstick is now in focus. The recent “State of State Finances 2026-27” report by PRS Legislative Research shows that state goods and services tax (SGST) revenue growth slowed relative to gross domestic product (GDP) growth in FY26 for the first time in four years. SGST as a share of gross state domestic product (GSDP) fell in 23 states.
 
SGST is estimated to account for about 44 per cent of states’ OTR in FY27.
 
The question is how responsive a state’s OTR is to growth in nominal GSDP. This responsiveness is called tax buoyancy. In recent years, it has been slipping.
 
In FY25, only four of 28 states had a tax buoyancy above 1: Manipur, Punjab, Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra.
 
A tax buoyancy above 1 means that tax revenue is growing faster than the economy. It can point to a widening tax base and help states keep debt and deficits in check. Conversely, a buoyancy below 1 can indicate a narrow tax base.
 
Maharashtra benefited mainly from its high domestic consumption and large services sector. Chhattisgarh, a mineral-rich state, and agriculture-led Punjab also saw revenue grow faster than their economies. Manipur recorded the highest buoyancy, at 2 in FY25, but a decade ago its tax revenue did not even keep pace with its economy.
 
In FY25, Telangana was the only state with negative buoyancy. It indicates its tax revenue fell even as its economy grew.
 
Between FY16 and FY25, 12 of the 28 states improved their buoyancy, while 16 slipped. The states that most often outpaced their economies were mostly northeastern: Arunachal Pradesh (seven years), and Manipur, Nagaland, Mizoram and Telangana (six years each).
 
In FY16, 11 states had a tax buoyancy above 1. Arunachal Pradesh topped the list at over 5, followed by Chhattisgarh at 4.76. Odisha, Mizoram, Bihar and Telangana recorded buoyancies between 2.5 and 3. 
 
Over the decade since FY16, the number of states with tax buoyancy above 1 peaked in FY23 at 23 of the 28 states. It then dropped to 11 in FY24 and just four in FY25. The count fell to single digits in FY17, FY20 and FY25. 
 
The states’ tax buoyancy has been declining since FY23, falling from 1.43 in FY23 to 0.92 in FY24 and 0.67 in FY25. The buoyancy of the Union government’s gross tax revenue also declined over the same period, but it exceeded that of the states in both FY24 and FY25. 
 
States’ OTR now accounts for more than half of their revenue receipts, yet collections are growing more slowly than their economies. States that want fiscal self-reliance will need to widen their tax base and push OTR growth.

data.title: RBI lets rupee rise to break one-way bets on further depreciation
data.description:
India's central bank is using the return of foreign inflows to break bets on a one-way slide in the rupee, allowing the currency to strengthen rather than buying dollars to rebuild reserves.

The strategy ​could encourage exporters to sell more dollars, reduce hedging by importers and ease foreign investors' ​concerns over currency losses, analysts and two sources familiar with the Reserve Bank of India's thinking said.

Indian equities have drawn a ‌record $16 billion in foreign inflows in November, reversing nearly two years of selling and providing the central bank an opportunity to rebuild reserves.

Yet, the RBI has largely stayed out of the currency market despite an $80 billion drawdown in reserves from their $785.7 billion peak, following heavy dollar sales in October to defend the rupee as it approached its record low of 96.96 per dollar.

 

The RBI's dollar purchases during the rupee's recovery have been limited despite around $40 billion in forward commitments maturing over the next year, Dhiraj Nim, FX strategist and senior economist at ANZ Bank, said.

"We think its immediate priority is to put exporter hedging on a sustained footing and ease forward market imbalances (between importer and exporter hedging)," he added.

"That may require further rupee appreciation."

Nim said the rupee would face stiff resistance at 90-91 per dollar. The currency traded at 92.62 on Friday.

The RBI is in "no hurry" to rebuild reserves and could allow ‌the rupee to appreciate while replenishing reserves if inflows persist, one of the sources said, requesting anonymity due to restrictions on speaking to the media.

The strategy is consistent with Governor Sanjay Malhotra's publicly stated view that the rupee was undervalued.

An RBI spokesperson did not respond to an email seeking comment on the currency strategy.

EARLY SIGNS OF RESET

The rupee fell 4.8% in 2025 and another 5.5% in the first 10 months of this year, pressured by nearly $50 billion in foreign equity outflows amid India's limited exposure to the AI investment boom and steep valuations.

Persistent weakness prompted foreign investors to build short rupee positions in the offshore non-deliverable forwards market, exporters to retain dollar earnings and ​importers to step up hedging.

The resulting spiral prompted the RBI to curb open currency positions, impose reserve requirements on large hedging transactions and allow ‌oil companies to buy dollars directly from its reserves.

With the rupee now up more than 4% from its lows, expectations are shifting.

Exporter hedging volumes over the past week were significantly higher than levels seen throughout the year, the head of markets at ​a large private-sector bank ‌said, citing renewed hedging of future dollar receivables by Indian IT companies.

Investors turned bullish on the rupee for the first time in 18 months, ‌helped by record foreign equity inflows and lower oil prices, a Reuters poll showed on Thursday.

FLEXIBILITY ON RATES

A sustained recovery in the rupee would provide the RBI higher flexibility to focus monetary policy on domestic growth and inflation conditions, rather than having to ‌contend with ​currency weakness. This, ​in turn, could strengthen the rupee's fundamental support.

"Credible moves" on interest rates to address domestic sources of inflation would do more to ease underlying pressures on the rupee, said Aaron Hurd, senior portfolio manager for currency at State Street ‌Investment Management.

"We need to see ​2-3 more rate hikes over the coming quarters, preferably front-loaded with a hike at each of the next two meetings."

data.title: Axis MF launches Nifty LargeMidcap 250 Index Fund: NFO dates, key details
data.description:
Investors looking for exposure to both large-cap and mid-cap stocks through a single passive fund can consider a new offering from Axis Mutual Fund, which has launched the Axis Nifty LargeMidcap 250 Index Fund. The new fund offer (NFO) opens on November 27 and will remain open until December 11, 2026.
 
The open-ended index fund will track the Nifty LargeMidcap 250 Total Return Index (TRI), subject to tracking error. It will invest in a portfolio designed to mirror the index, which combines large-cap and mid-cap stocks in equal proportions.
 

What are the key features of the Axis Nifty LargeMidcap 250 Index Fund?

- NFO period: November 27 to December 11, 2026
 
- Benchmark: Nifty LargeMidcap 250 TRI
- Fund managers: Nandik Mallik and Rohit Gautam
- Minimum investment: ₹100, followed by investments in multiples of ₹1
- Allocation: 50 per cent to large-cap stocks and 50 per cent to mid-cap stocks
- Exit load: 0.25 per cent if redeemed or switched out within 15 days of allotment; nil thereafter
- Riskometer: Very High

What does the Nifty LargeMidcap 250 Index offer?

 
The Nifty LargeMidcap 250 Index comprises 100 companies from the Nifty 100 and 150 companies from the Nifty Midcap 150. Together, these stocks represent approximately 75 per cent of India's listed market capitalisation, according to Axis Mutual Fund.
 
The index maintains a 50:50 allocation between large-cap and mid-cap stocks, with weights reset quarterly to maintain this balance. This means investors get exposure to established businesses as well as mid-sized companies that may be expanding their operations and market presence.
 
The index also has relatively lower concentration in its largest constituents. As of October 30, 2026, its top 10 stocks accounted for around 22 per cent of the index, compared with 43 per cent in the Nifty 100 and 53 per cent in the Nifty 50, according to the fund house.
 

How has the Nifty LargeMidcap 250 Index performed?

 
Over the 10-year period ended October 30, 2026, the Nifty LargeMidcap 250 TRI delivered a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 13.8 per cent, according to Axis Mutual Fund.
 
In comparison, the Nifty 100 TRI returned 11.7 per cent and the Nifty 50 TRI 11.6 per cent over the same period, the fund house said.
 
Past performance may or may not be sustained in the future and does not indicate the returns investors can expect from the new fund.
 

What should investors consider before investing?

 
The fund follows a passive strategy, meaning it will seek to replicate the index rather than actively select stocks in an attempt to outperform it. Its returns, before expenses, will aim to correspond with those of the benchmark, subject to tracking error.
 
A 50 per cent allocation to mid-caps can expose investors to greater volatility and liquidity risks than a portfolio dominated by large-cap stocks. While the index spreads investments across 250 companies, its returns can still be affected by market downturns, particularly when mid-cap stocks face sharper corrections.
 
Investors should also consider whether they already have exposure to large-cap and mid-cap stocks through other mutual funds. Adding another fund with similar holdings may not necessarily improve portfolio diversification.
 
The scheme and its benchmark are both categorised as Very High risk on the Riskometer, according to the fund house.
 
The fund is intended for investors seeking long-term equity exposure through a passive strategy, but investors should assess their risk tolerance, investment horizon and existing portfolio allocation before investing.

data.title: US could hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site if strikes resume: Trump
data.description:
US President Donald Trump has warned that the United States could target Iran's underground Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility if it launches fresh military strikes, even as he claimed that Washington had victory within reach and was allowing Tehran to reach a deal, ANI reported.
 
Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida on Thursday (local time), Trump said the US had not detected significant activity at the facility but would strike it if military action resumed.
 
“If we did anything, we would absolutely hit Pickaxe Mountain, but we haven't seen any real activity there,” Trump said.
 
Pickaxe Mountain is a heavily fortified underground facility near Iran's Natanz uranium enrichment complex. The site has emerged as a potential target amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict.
 
 
Trump's remarks came during a series of Thanksgiving calls with American military personnel, alongside First Lady Melania Trump. During the interaction, he claimed that Iran's military capabilities had been severely weakened and said Washington was still allowing Tehran to negotiate.
 
“We have victory at hand. It will happen whenever I want it to happen. We are trying to be nice. We are giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives, but I am not sure if they are going to take advantage of that,” Trump said.
 
He also claimed that Iran's air force and navy had been wiped out and that Tehran had been unable to resume operations at nuclear facilities previously targeted by the US.
 
Trump further said that Iran had missiles capable of reaching Europe, while reiterating that preventing Tehran from acquiring nuclear weapons remained a key US objective.

Iran says diplomacy remains an option

Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi said Tehran remained open to diplomacy but was currently prioritising the country's resilience against external pressure and efforts to maintain trade routes.
 
In an interview with state news agency IRNA, Araghchi said Iranian officials, particularly those stationed in neighbouring countries, were working to ensure that the country's requirements were met and trade routes remained operational.
 
“Our main focus is on the country's resilience and helping to increase resilience against the pressures that enemies apply through various means,” he said.
 
Addressing the possibility of negotiations with Washington, Araghchi said diplomacy remained part of Iran's approach, but added that countering sanctions and external pressure was a more immediate priority.
 
“Negotiation is part of our work, and we have not forgotten it, and we are pursuing it; but in the current situation, there is also a more important mission, and that is to discourage the enemies from the sanctions and pressures they are imposing on our country,” he said.
 
Araghchi also confirmed that mediation efforts by Qatar and Pakistan were continuing, with both countries conveying proposals and suggestions to Tehran.

Iran accuses Israel of pushing for fresh conflict

In a separate interview with Shahrara News, Araghchi accused Israel of making statements intended to create an atmosphere conducive to another conflict and draw Washington into a fresh war with Tehran.
 
He alleged that Israel was making claims about Iran to justify further military action, adding that the country remained prepared to defend itself.
 
Araghchi also claimed that American public opinion was increasingly recognising what he described as the prioritisation of Israeli interests over those of the US.
 
(With inputs from ANI)

data.title: Gold, silver prices extend rebound on strong buying at lower levels
data.description:
Gold and silver prices rose sharply on Friday, November 27, as buying at lower levels and short covering followed a steep recent decline. However, strong US economic data and the Federal Reserve’s hawkish stance kept concerns over further interest-rate increases alive.
 
At the time of writing, gold futures on Comex were trading near $3,630 per ounce, while silver was trading near $43.40 per ounce.
 
In the domestic market, gold futures on the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) were trading near ₹1,23,900 per 10 gram, while silver futures were trading near ₹1,51,400 per kg.

Gold prices rise

Gold futures opened higher. On the MCX, the benchmark December gold contract opened ₹2,028 higher at ₹1,24,300 per 10 gram. The previous close was ₹1,22,272.
 
 
At the time of writing, the contract was trading ₹1,612 higher at ₹1,23,884.
 
Gold futures had touched a high of ₹1,59,700 per 10 gram earlier this year.

Silver jumps above ₹1.5 lakh

Silver futures also opened sharply higher. On the MCX, the benchmark December silver contract opened ₹5,833 higher at ₹1,51,676 per kg. The previous close was ₹1,45,843.
 
At the time of writing, the contract was trading ₹5,551 higher at ₹1,51,394.
 
Silver futures had touched a high of ₹4,20,048 per kg earlier this year.

Gold, silver jump in global market

Gold and silver were trading sharply higher in the international market.
 
On Comex, gold opened at $3,590.30 per ounce. The previous closing price was $3,535.80. At the time of writing, it was trading $96.20 higher at $3,632 per ounce.
 
Gold prices had touched a high of $5,586.20 per ounce earlier this year.
 
Comex silver futures opened at $41.27 per ounce. The previous closing price was $40.05. At the time of writing, silver was trading $3.38 higher at $43.43 per ounce.
 
Silver prices had touched a high of $121.79 per ounce earlier this year.

Is the rebound in gold and silver gathering pace?

Anindya Banerjee, head of commodity and currency research at Kotak Neo, said silver was leading the rebound that had been expected after the heavy sell-off in precious metals.
 
Gold had fallen below $3,500 per ounce on Wednesday for the first time since September 2025, but recovered above that level within the same trading session. Before the Indian market opened on Friday, gold had risen to around $3,630 per ounce, a gain of nearly 2 per cent. Silver was up around 5 per cent near $43.70 per ounce.
 
Ajay Kedia, director, Kedia Advisory, said gold and silver had recovered as equity markets stabilised and selling pressure eased.
 
However, expectations of a US Federal Reserve rate increase in December could limit the upside, he said.

Levels to watch

According to Kedia, gold was technically witnessing short covering. Open interest declined 16.4 per cent to 6,517 contracts, while prices rose by ₹1,135.
 
Gold has support at ₹1,21,200, followed by ₹1,20,140.
 
The technical data placed resistance at ₹1,23,610, followed by ₹1,24,960. However, the current gold price quoted in the report, at ₹1,23,884, has already crossed the first resistance level, bringing the next level into focus.
 
Silver was also witnessing short covering. Open interest declined 5.29 per cent to 9,056 contracts, while prices rose by ₹3,326.
 
Silver has support at ₹1,44,470, followed by ₹1,43,100.
 
The technical data placed resistance at ₹1,48,010, followed by ₹1,50,170. However, the current silver price quoted in the report, at ₹1,51,394, has already crossed both resistance levels.

MCX, Comex prices

  
Note: MCX gold futures prices are in rupees per 10 gram, while MCX silver futures prices are in rupees per kg. Comex gold and silver futures prices are in dollars per ounce. Last traded prices are as of the time of writing.
